findings.rule: 093 User Flow (D: review_model configured? No -> F: exit review_model_required)
findings.evidence: configured_model() falls back to the first review_reviewers entry when review_model is unset. The spec flowchart goes straight from 'review_model configured? No' to review_model_required. review_reviewers holds the plan-review cascade (the README example starts with google/gemini-3.1-pro), so a project with no review_model gets its goals, lanes and progressions bound to that cascade model and not to the native reviewer. That is the 'select another identity' problem the spec describes. Also, review_model: default does not fall through to the reviewers list. It goes straight to review_model_required.
findings.correction: Pick one option. (a) Record the review_reviewers fallback in spec 093 as an Edge Case or in the AC-001 wording, so the spec matches the code and README. (b) Make resolve_review_identity read only review_model and keep the reviewers fallback only in current_review_model for plan-review cascades.

findings.rule: 093 Edge Cases (budget out of bounds refused); plan D-01
findings.evidence: This change adds a new upper bound, REVIEW_MAX_CHARS_MAX = 200000. Spec and plan only say out-of-bounds budgets are refused and never define the bounds. Before this change, prepare_feature_review accepted any configured review_max_chars >= 1000, and the --review-max-chars options in cli.py and pipeline.py keep min=1000 with no maximum. A project with review_max_chars above 200000 now fails every review path: validate --prepare-review, orchestrator, semantic_analysis, lane, progression and revision matches_commit. The constants also duplicate the ge=1000/le=200000 bounds in validator/execution_mapping.py:43 instead of sharing them.
findings.correction: Add the 1000..200000 inclusive bounds to the 093 spec Edge Cases. Import the bounds from one shared constant used by both execution_mapping and review_identity_config. Optionally add max=200000 to the --review-max-chars typer options so explicit values give the same error everywhere.

findings.rule: 093 AC-001 scope vs 086 AC (prepare/verify exit codes)
findings.evidence: AC-001 replaces the 086 behavior only for `livespec delivery lane`. Through _lane(), `delivery review prepare` and `delivery review verify` now also exit 2 with review_model_required when no model resolves, and revision open/close exit 1. Spec 086 says verify exits 0 or 1 with a closed list of codes. With no model, verify used to check the full lane and could pass. This extension is documented in system/review-protocol.md but not in the 093 spec.
findings.correction: Extend 093 AC-001 (or add an edge case) to cover `delivery review prepare|verify` and `delivery revision open|close`, with their exit codes, so the 086 contract change is specified.
